_comment: Consensus: Praos, TPraos and PBFT, chain selection, the hard-fork combinator's state and history, header rules (module consensus). Its reference is ouroboros-consensus, and cardano-ledger for the protocol rules (cardano-protocol-tpraos). docs/design/correspondence-map.md says what an entry holds; scripts/check_correspondence.py checks it.

def consensus.leios.LeiosCertification.c.note: the CertRB path of applyBlock's ApplyVal up to the closure: the parent's announcement, announcingRbHash, leiosCommitteeOfTip and verifyLeiosCert in that order, each failing with its LeiosExtValidationError, all on the unticked parent; a pure function of those inputs returning the verdict, where the reference runs it inside its ExceptT before resolveAndApplyLeiosClosure, and a typed defect for what the reference cannot hold; the two FIXME checks are not run, as there. The fixture suite runs it on the testnet's certifying block 97,276 from its parent's state

def consensus.leios.LeiosCertification.a.note: announcementLeiosPoint of protocolStateLeiosAnnouncement, composed: a Praos2 state's announcement at fromWithOrigin (SlotNo 0) praosStateLastSlot, none for the states of the other protocols; the election's issuer and the body size, which the point does not carry, are not kept

def consensus.leios.LeiosCertification.l.note: the ledger view at the state's own tip reduced to the two fields getLeiosCommitteeFromView reads: the set snapshot's committee and unboundRational of the current ppLeiosQuorumStakeThreshold in Dijkstra, none in the eras before it; read from the NewEpochState directly rather than through ledgerViewOfTip's forecast, which at its own anchor projects the same state; a Dijkstra state of the 11.1 layout, which the Leios build cannot hold, is a defect. The fixture suite reads the testnet's committee of epoch 100 with it, under which block 97,276's certificate verifies

def consensus.ByronRulesConfig#windowThr.note: the threshold field of pbftWindowParams, for the configured signature threshold and a window its caller gives (ByronRules.update gives k, as pbftWindowSize does); the reference builds the window size and the threshold together from its configuration, and the floor into a Word64 is ByronRules.windowThreshold's, whose results the suite compares with values measured on GHC 9.10.3

def consensus.HardForkConfig#check.note: HeaderProtVerTooHigh is checked with the envelope here; the reference checks it in Conway's BBODY rule

def consensus.Praos2.State.newEpoch.note: the new-epoch branch of tickChainDepStatePolyPraos: the epoch nonce, the previous epoch nonce and the last epoch block nonce as the reference updates them, and the announcement cleared; the isNewEpoch decision is its callers' (Praos2.tick, and Praos.tick for a Praos2 state)

def consensus.state.EraHistory.perasRoun.note: the eraPerasRoundLength of each era's parameters, the per-era class method and constant merged into one function of the state layout (the Leios layout is one build's) and the era; no captured answer of the reference carries a Dijkstra round length yet, so the 90 slots are checked against the source only (LeiosBoundsSuite, LeiosBoundsEvidenceSuite's hand-derived GetInterpreter bytes)

def consensus.state.EraHistory.originLay.note: the Peras round of initBound only, by layout; the time, slot and epoch zero are the era history's (EraHistory.boundAt). The suite compares the genesis start's bounds with those of a state the Leios build wrote

def consensus.state.EraHistory.unrounded.note: the Peras round of mkUpperBound for an era of NoPerasEnabled; the suite compares the bound where Dijkstra starts, placed from Conway's start, with the first Dijkstra state the Leios build wrote

def consensus.state.EraHistory.upperLayo.note: the Peras round of mkUpperBound, its where clause (inEraEpochs by countEpochs, inEraSlots their product with the epoch size, both Word64, inEraPerasRounds the div by the round length) computed modulo 2^64 as the reference computes it; the branch of an era with rounds (Dijkstra) has no captured reference bound to compare with, only hand-derived cases (LeiosBoundsSuite)

def consensus.state.EraHistory.upperBoun.note: mkUpperBound whole: the slot the lower bound's plus inEraSlots modulo 2^64 (addSlots), the time the lower bound's plus those slots times the slot length, exact (addRelTime of a NominalDiffTime), the epoch as given and the round by upperLayout; the epoch size and slot length are given by the caller rather than an EraParams. EraStartSuite checks a wrapped bound against bytes derived from the source; as upperLayout, the rounds a Dijkstra end adds have no captured reference bound yet

def consensus.state.GenesisMirror.origin.note: the extended state's layout part at the chain's origin: the Leios build's Peras state of no epoch context and no certificate, which the captured Leios states hold (82 83 01 80 80 80); the 11.1 layout has none

def consensus.state.MirrorClock.interpre.note: reconstructSummary with the bounds of the state's layout: the past bounds and the current start from the telescope, the current era's end at the known transition or its safe zone, and the next era where the transition is known and the code has one, each computed by upperBound and safeZoneEnd with the reference's Word64 arithmetic; non-empty by construction (NonEmptyVector); no GetInterpreter answer of the Leios build has been captured, so its bytes are hand-derived (LeiosBoundsEvidenceSuite), and this node does not enter Dijkstra yet (#54)

def consensus.state.EraHistory.epochBoun.note: slotToEpochBound with the epoch size given rather than an EraParams; countSlots, the epochs + 1 and addEpochs are Word64, computed modulo 2^64

def consensus.state.EraHistory.safeZoneE.note: applySafeZone's StandardSafeZone case, with the era's parameters given one by one; no Cardano era has an UnsafeIndefiniteSafeZone in the summary the node answers with. QueryGoldenSuite compares GetInterpreter answers, whose ends it computes, with the reference node's

def consensus.state.EraHistory.unrounded.note: mkUpperBound of an era with no Peras rounds, the epoch size and slot length given rather than an EraParams: the slot modulo 2^64, the time exact, the round kept (Leios) or none (11.1). MirrorStep.startOf places an era entered after the start with it, as whenExtend does; LeiosBoundsEvidenceSuite compares that bound with the first Dijkstra state the Leios build wrote, QueryGoldenSuite the GetInterpreter ends with the reference node's

def consensus.DijkstraCrossing.forecastI.note: the Dijkstra forecast's three cases (the tip's own view, TICKF's view before the exclusive bound of the stability window past the tip's successor, OutsideForecastRange after it) as the reference's; the view holds only the fields header validation reads (Praos2.LedgerView), not the committee, the quorum or the transaction-byte bound. DijkstraHeaderRulesSuite validates the public testnet's headers after its ledger state at slot 2,168,639 against it, the leader check on that state's stake, and its exclusive bound

enum consensus.leios.LeiosTxsReplyFault.note: the Left strings of the two checks as a closed type; the reference raises them with error and the peer loses its connection

def consensus.leios.LeiosFetchLogic.batc.note: each request also names the pool its jobs were picked from (LeiosJobPoolId)

def consensus.HeaderChain#trimmedTo.note: the trim of intersectsWithCurrentChain: the candidate from the anchor of our chain on (AF.splitAfterPoint theirFrag (AF.anchorPoint ourFrag')), with the header state history trimmed alike. The reference trims when our chain changed and the candidate still intersects it; Scarab's gate trims after each recorded header, to the anchor of the selection published with the history (the one the header was validated against), keeps a chain that does not pass through the anchor for its reintersection to decide, and also drops the local prefix Scarab keeps for ChainSync jumping before that anchor

glue.reason: the Leios certification check's Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own: its companion, the committee of the tip decoded once into the BLS layer's (the reference's LeiosCommittee holds decoded keys, and leiosCommitteeOfTip returns it with the threshold as a pair), the value a passing certificate yields (the reference continues in place with the announced point), and what the committee is made of, by which the node keeps the committee it decoded for an equal basis (#73, #54)
the instances of Praos2's state types that the chain-dependent state derives its equality, rendering and difference from, and the companions that hold them: Scala plumbing with no counterpart (#826)

the acquired-endorser-block gate's Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own: the companions, the certificate's presence as an enum (biHasLeiosCert) and a block of the forest as the gate reads it (#54)

the Leios fetch state's Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own: the companions, Word32's conversions and order on BytesSize, the MultiSet operations on FocusedEbs, the orders as Scala Orderings, the equalities, the job id's constructor, and the decision's result triple as a named record (#54)

the id of a pool of an endorser block's jobs and the key of a peer's jobs in flight by endorser block and pool, the Improvement approved on 2026-11-22 (https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/54#issuecomment-7076220269): the reference's transactions request names its jobs by number alone and keys a peer's jobs in flight by the endorser block alone, so these types, the first id and the equality have no counterpart (#54)
the companions holding the pure roll-forward functions and the announcement's equality instance: Scala plumbing with no counterpart (#54)

the mirror's plumbing for a Dijkstra block on the era types, which holds no flat block: the step of MirrorStep.block with the transaction bytes given, and the era history's horizon at the tip that the era rules' UTxO context reads as its EpochInfo (#54)

the routing of a Dijkstra block's defects to the follower's no verdict, where valid peer input can meet a limit of this build, or to a stop (BlockNoVerdict.ofDijkstra, #54): the node's own, as BlockNoVerdict is (issue 567); the reference has no path without a verdict

the Leios voting's Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own: the companion of the decisions, a voting key kept with the verification key derived from it once (deriveVerKeyDSIGN in goVote), the capability goVote runs over and the view of the selection it reads (the reference's forker at the volatile tip), the typed outcome of decideLeiosCertify (the reference returns Maybe and traces), and the defects that are the reference's error calls (decideLeiosCertify's on genesis its own) or a native library failure (#54)

a restored Dijkstra state's snapshot sidecar parameter records, held beside the mirror in memory so the sidecar is written again as it was read (the fields of the eras before Dijkstra, which Dijkstra's governance state has no place for, as the import wrote them), Dijkstra's own fields the governance state's; the reference's snapshot has no such sidecar, so this has no counterpart (#826)
The LeiosTxCache index's empty index over orderings it is given, so that a test can count the comparisons of its maps; the node takes the byte orderings (#54).

the orders a peer's jobs in flight are kept in (requestedJobsPerPeer as an ordered map, as the reference's Map): a pool id by its count, and a pool of an endorser block by the block's hash bytes then the pool's id; Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own, the pool id being part of the approved Improvement of LeiosJobPoolId (#54)

The Conway switch (#85): the no verdict a Conway block's defect is (BlockNoVerdict.ofConway, issue 567's routing, which the reference has no counterpart of), and the one value Conway's era rules read their system start, epoch information and slot to time translation from (MirrorClock.conway, the era history of MirrorClock.of for a Conway block, not extended).

the Scala plumbing of the indexed AnchoredFragment and HeaderChain with no counterpart of their own: the position lookups and cuts the candidate's states are aligned by, structural equality, hashing and rendering over the points and fields alone, the companions and instances, the fields HeaderChain had as a case class with the constructor that indexes them and a copy that indexes only changed points, and the candidate's points as the density rule's fragment without collecting them again (#810)

the selected chain's index by hash, which chain selection's walks over the processed forest read to tell a selected block and the places a block's predecessor names, where the reference compares points on its AnchoredFragment; Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own (#810)
